submitted.rationale: Index 74 (Bi 0.07, Cu 0.54, V 0.39) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 1.7e-7 A, at 2.06 eV. Its Cu/V ratio (~1.4) is close to a Cu3V2O8-type vanadate. MEGNet gaps place such phases between CuO (0.3 eV) and V2O5 (2.8 eV), so they can absorb 602 nm light. The neighboring index 73, which has less Cu, gave less (1.2e-7 A).

rejected.reason: Measured 0 A. This Cu-rich, V-poor composition probably forms CuO or CuBi2O4 (CuO HSE gap 0.3 eV), which is recombination-dominated or p-type.
Measured 1.2e-7 A, lower than 74. The Cu/V ratio closer to 1:1 performed worse.
The V2O5 HSE gap is 2.83 eV and BiVO4 is about 2.4 eV, both above the 2.06 eV photon energy. These were not measured.

consultations.verdict: Weak support. MEGNet HSE gap for Cu2O (mp-361) is 1.56 eV, below the 2.06 eV photon energy, so Cu-rich oxides should absorb at 602 nm. BiVO4 (~2.4 eV) would not. Candidate 74 has Cu/V near 3:2 (a Cu3V2O8-type vanadate with a gap of about 1.8–2 eV), so it is a sensible first probe of the Cu-vanadate photoanode region. I could not get IDs for the ternary phases, so this is indirect evidence.

Support for moving away from the V-rich corner. The V2O5 (mp-25279) HSE gap is 2.83 eV, which is well above 2.06 eV, so V-rich compositions should absorb poorly at 602 nm. Cu-rich phases with smaller gaps are preferred. Candidate 108 (Bi 0.28, Cu 0.55, V 0.18) is the closest candidate to the BiCu2VO6 stoichiometry, a known narrow-gap photoanode, so it tests a different phase region from 74.

Mixed, leaning support. The CuO (mp-704645) HSE gap is 0.32 eV, which means CuO absorbs strongly but acts as a recombination center or p-type phase. That fits the zero photocurrent at the Cu-rich, V-poor index 108, where CuO or CuBi2O4 would form. Photocurrent is only likely where V is plentiful enough to form Cu vanadates with gaps between those of CuO (0.3 eV) and V2O5 (2.8 eV). Index 74 was active, and 73 is its neighbor with Cu/V closer to 1:1 (β-Cu2V2O7-like). The GP also gives 73 the highest mean.
